title: Answer Abatement in Granted Employer Benefit Charging Protests: Case Notes
content:
**Rule (Employer Benefit Charging).** The answer abatement is four fifths when no separation response to the notice of claim is on record for the position, nine tenths when the separation response on record was received after the response due date without good cause, and the whole otherwise.

| Response to the notice of claim | Answer abatement |
|---|---|
| No separation response on record for the position | 0.80 (four fifths) |
| Separation response on record, received after the response due date, without good cause | 0.90 (nine tenths) |
| Any other case | 1.00 (the whole) |

A separation response is on record when the employer's submissions on the position include a separation-response submission. Whether it was received after the due date is read from the response date and the response due date recorded on the position; a response recorded as late with good cause shown is not without good cause.

## Late responses and the class term

For a protest decision the class term that payments issued before a late response stay charged even if relief is later granted is applied only through the answer abatement: a separation response received after the response due date without good cause abates the relief credit, and no payment is kept charged on that account beyond it.

## Case notes (hypothetical positions)

**Case 1.** The notice of claim was never answered; the employer's submissions on the position show only a protest. No separation response is on record: abatement 0.80.

**Case 2.** The response due date was 13 March; the response date on the position is 17 March and the response is recorded as late, with no good cause. Abatement 0.90.

**Case 3.** Same dates as Case 2, but the response is recorded as late with good cause shown. Abatement 1.00.

**Case 4.** The response due date was 13 March and the response was received on 13 March. It was not received after the due date: abatement 1.00.
